events.title: Go 1.0 released
events.summary: Google released Go 1.0 on March 28, 2012 — promising long-term compatibility and a production-ready toolchain for systems and cloud software.
events.about: Go 1.0 committed to the Go 1 compatibility promise: code written for 1.0 should compile on future 1.x releases. It powered Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, and countless microservices with goroutines, static binaries, and fast compiles.

narrative.whyChosen: Go 1.0 was the stability milestone that let companies bet on Go for infrastructure.
narrative.whyImportant: The compatibility guarantee made Go viable for long-lived server and DevOps tooling.
narrative.problemSolved: Early Go changed rapidly; production teams needed a frozen language spec and standard library.

events.title: webpack first released
events.summary: Tobias Koppers published webpack 0.1.0 on March 10, 2012 — a module bundler that assembles JavaScript, CSS, and assets for the browser.
events.about: webpack traces `import` dependencies into a dependency graph and emits optimized bundles — with code splitting, loaders, and plugins. It powered the React, Vue, and Angular build pipelines of the 2010s before Vite and esbuild. Example: split vendor and app chunks, tree-shake dead code, and hot-reload during development.

narrative.whyChosen: webpack defined how frontend teams shipped modular JavaScript before native ES modules dominated.
narrative.whyImportant: It made npm packages composable in the browser and set expectations for dev servers and production builds.
narrative.problemSolved: Browsers could not load hundreds of separate npm modules efficiently; apps needed one optimized artifact.

events.title: Composer first released
events.summary: Nils Adermann and Jordi Boggiano released Composer 1.0.0-alpha1 on March 1, 2012 — a dependency manager for PHP inspired by npm and Bundler.
events.about: Composer reads `composer.json`, resolves versions from Packagist, and installs packages into `vendor/` with an autoloader — `composer require symfony/http-foundation` adds a library and its dependencies. It modernized PHP the way npm modernized Node. Example: declare PSR-4 autoloading and run `composer install` in CI for reproducible deploys.

narrative.whyChosen: Composer brought semver dependency management to PHP after years of PEAR and manual includes.
narrative.whyImportant: It enabled a modern PHP ecosystem with Laravel, Symfony, and thousands of reusable packages.
narrative.problemSolved: PHP projects copied vendor code by hand or used brittle global PEAR installs.
